items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: He was my best teacher. He gave me information that nobody else would give, now I’m just giving it back.

ctx.x: I teach two ensemble courses, and that is undergraduate ensemble courses. There are all kinds of elective classes that the kids can take. But the ensemble classes are classes that give them a chance to learn about jazz. Most of them don’t know anything about jazz. But whatever they can do when they’re undergraduate people, they’re allowed to take this elective class. And when they come in I don’t know what instruments they’re going to play, it could be clarinet, alto, tenor, it could be a French horn, it could be…

same way they taught me at Juilliard. I had some excellent teachers. Gordon Stanley would give me pieces that I thought I’d never be able to play. And I’d get to like say after three weeks of playing and still wasn’t there, and he’d ask me to come out to his house. He lived in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania and I’d come out to his house. And he had private students. And I’d be up in the attic, in that hot attic, practicing on that dummy keyboard. Then when I’d come down and play for him he would correct all the things I…
And I see your son has a thing out now, he’s a singer?
